title: Getting a Move On When the Louvre's Bombed

source_quality.notes: Text layer is real. Displayed formulas were checked on rendered pages 6 and 13. Section 8.1 ends mid-sentence. The mu formula's exponent sign disagrees with the prose.

task_reconstruction.problem_statement: Design and test exit-sign directions so visitors leave the Louvre and responders still reach a target when the building is crowded or damaged.
sub_tasks: Build a room graph from a public floor plan
Find connectivity bottlenecks by a spectral cut
Guess hidden exits by minimizing mean distance
Simulate individual movement with congestion and blocking
Approximate the same flow by a density ODE
Test damage, crowd distribution and extra exits
Recommend a sign policy and a search procedure
task_reconstruction.data_provided: No contest dataset. A public floor plan annotated by hand, a 2017 visitor rate, a footprint area and a safety-code capacity.

edges.via: the same penalty and blocking idea

unresolved_questions: Does mu = t_0 exp(+c rho) slow people or speed them? The prose says slower.
What are t_0, c and the critical dead-end density?
Does the factor n double-count the exponential already written in the scalar flow?
Section 8.1 stops mid-sentence. Was a policy sentence cut?

section_map.summary: Signs are the plan. Three stages: overview, agent check, fast ODE.
The one shared object is an exit plan.
Hand-annotated floor plan, nearly equal edge lengths.
Hidden exits guessed by flood fill.
Erlang to exponential, density penalty, blocking.
Continuum analogue with blocking and non-negativity.
Time rises with density, falls with exits, ignores room mix.
Nearest door is a guess; search before you trust it.

contributions.summary: A computed Cheeger interval and a four-corridor Fiedler cut that isolates the Richelieu wing.
A discrete-event evacuation with refused entry at capacity and a smaller penalty for responders.
Exit time is sensitive to head count, door count and connectivity, not to which rooms start full.

assumptions.summary: Visitors follow signs and signs stay visible.
At high density, congestion dominates distance.
Hidden exits were placed to minimize mean path length.
A crowd may be treated as a shear-thickening fluid. The footnote says stress means force per area.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Public floor plan, hand annotated, room size and adjacency typed in.
2532.83 arrivals per hour in 2017, times a 3 hour visit, gives 7598.49 people. Footprint 72735 m^2 caps safe occupancy at 21748.

verification.summary: Responder travel time averaged across trials against five arrival delays and nine densities.
Each model is given one job and refused another. No shared numeric test.

results_trace.summary: The sign cut severs 4 corridors and isolates Richelieu from every exit.
At density 0.3 the slow arrival is near 5 minutes; at 0.65 near 10. Immediate entry is faster at every density tried.
More exits shorten clearance. A nonuniform start does not. Cut links hurt sharply when density is high.

writing_logic.summary: Roadmap before any equation: overview, then the simulation that checks it, then a faster stand-in.
A limitation list is the reason the next model exists.
The recommendation is a search the client should run, not a sign plan the team already found.

language_observations.summary: progresses as such / Next / Then, and the baseline is called a heuristic guess.
the one congruity; Indeed, common ground; Thus, our analysis works to identify.
Spoken loop: If we can we, move that person. If not, add another random number.
Footnote disarms shear stress: one would imagine, but here we mean force over area.
could best be understood as average behavior, then the admission that tuning failed.

visualization_observations.summary: Room graph colored by distance to the nearest of four exits. Layout, not a flow result.
Fiedler coordinates and a histogram the authors call roughly bimodal.
3D partition: large nodes versus small nodes, the Richelieu cut.
Schematic of a blocked vertex and the schedules on its edges.
Grouped bars: responder time against density, five delay colors, averaged over trials.
Room densities after a time, with a middle band called equilibrium.
Density sketch piled on the Mona Lisa room.
Seconds to congestion by room, spikes at rooms that jam at once, compared as exits are added.
Full-evacuation time against setup, averaged over trials.

weaknesses.summary: The printed rate mu = t_0 exp(c rho) grows with density while the prose says movement gets harder. As written, the formula speeds people up.
The scalar flow already carries exp(-c rho), and n_i carries it again.
The future-work sentence on breaking up groups is cut off.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: A floor plan used as a graph, with a cut read back onto named corridors.
A density ODE on a directed room graph, stepped by Euler.
One factor dropped out (room mix) and three did not (head count, doors, connectivity).
Advice is a procedure the museum runs, with an upper bound the museum sets.
Responder delay is discussed only inside the densities the chart shows, and left as may.

independent_extensions.summary: If the penalty is meant to slow movement, the exponent on mu should be negative, matching the scalar flow. The paper never reconciles the two signs.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Awarded paper recommends a search it did not run and admits a model it could not tune. Coexists with Outstanding; not evidence that judges reward unfinished optimization.
